result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers swap the trapezoids for left-aligned bars on one scale, and every count and percentage in both is correct. A states what the percentages are relative to and leaves visible placeholders for the unit, period, as-of date and source. Its title also names the steepest drop. B separates the largest absolute loss (download to account, 4,500 users) from the weakest step rate, which is useful, but it never asks for the data source or period. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers replace the trapezoids with bars on a shared left baseline, and every figure in both is arithmetically correct. B is better on two points: its title and accent colour point straight at the steepest drop (setup to paid), and it adds a provenance line with placeholders for unit, period, date and source, which A leaves out. B also shows a single percentage column in the main view, so it is a little more selective.
